name: data-grid
origin: reui.io (https://reui.io/docs/components/base/data-grid, MIT), via EMITTE; rendering rebuilt on react-aria Table
description: A data grid driven by a TanStack Table v9 instance and rendered with react-aria's `Table`, which brings cell keyboard navigation, `aria-sort`, selection, column resizing, row drag and drop and virtualization. Create the table with `useTable({ features: dataGridFeatures, ... })`: the exported features cover sorting, filtering with facets, pagination, selection, row expanding (tree rows from `getSubRows`), row and column pinning, ordering, visibility and sizing, with client-side row models; for server-side data (or to show every row) set `manualSorting`/`manualFiltering`/`manualPagination`. Column `meta` takes `headerTitle`, `skeleton`, `autoSize`, `headerClassName` and `cellClassName`. Wrap parts in `DataGrid table={table} recordCount={…}`: `DataGridTable`, `DataGridPagination`, `DataGridColumnHeader` (sort indicator, plus a menu for pinning, moving and visibility when `tableLayout` enables them), `DataGridColumnVisibility`, `DataGridColumnFilter` (faceted, use `filterFn: "arrHas"`), `DataGridRowSelect` (with `enableRowSelection`), `DataGridRowPin` (pins to the top, or the bottom with `position="bottom"`), `DataGridRowActions` (a row's actions as `DropdownMenuItem`s behind a menu button, named from `rowLabel`; it doesn't trigger `onRowClick`, and with no items it shows a disabled "no actions" entry), `DataGridRowDragHandle` (with `onRowsReorder`) and `DataGridRowExpand` (shows `getSubRows` children, indented by depth, or with `getRowCanExpand` and `DataGridTable`'s `renderExpandedRow` a full-width details row). `onRowClick` makes rows actionable (click or Enter) and `onRowHover` fires when the pointer enters a row, e.g. to prefetch its details. Pinned cells and sticky headers paint `--data-grid-surface` (else `--card` inside a Card, else `--background`) and carry `data-pinned`/`data-last-col`. `tableLayout.columnsDraggable` lets users drag headers to reorder columns (keyboard users use the header menu's move actions; pinned columns stay put). `isLoading` shows skeleton rows (`meta.skeleton`) or a spinner; `meta.autoSize` columns take the remaining width (not measured from content). `DataGridTable`'s `footerContent` takes footer rows (`DataGridTableFootRow` with `DataGridTableFootRowCell`, `colSpan` to span columns; `tableLayout.footerBackground` tints them). The `i18n` prop on `DataGrid` replaces every built-in string (`{ labels: { sortAscending, rowsPerPage, paginationInfo: ({ from, to, count }) => …, goToPage: (page) => …, … } }`, defaults in `defaultDataGridI18n`); specific props like `emptyMessage` or the pagination labels still win. Infinite scroll: `DataGridTable`'s `onFetchMore` fires near the end of the loaded rows (`fetchMoreScrollOffset`, in viewport heights), `isFetchingMore` shows a loading row and `hasMore={false}` stops it with `allRowsLoadedMessage`; works with `isVirtualized`. `tableClassNames` adds classes to parts of the table (`base`, `header`, `headerSticky`, `body`, `bodyRow`, `footer`, `edgeCell`); `tableLayout` also takes `rowRounded`, `headerBorder` and `columnsResizeMode` ("onEnd" commits the width on release and draws a line at the pointer while dragging).
